p: roasted grains and nuts on Passover eve,
so that they will not sleep and … they will ask
so that they will not sleep and also so they will ask
They said about Rabbi Akiva that he would distribute roasted grains and nuts to children on Passover eve,
so that they would not sleep and … they would ask.
so that they would not sleep and so they would ask.
Rabbi Eliezer says: One grabs the matzot on the nights of Passover. … on account of the children, … so … they will not sleep
Rabbi Eliezer says: One grabs the matzot on the nights of Passover. One should eat them very quickly on account of the children, so that, due to the hasty consumption of the meal, they will not sleep

p: They said about Rabbi Akiva … in
except for the eves of Passover and the eve of Yom Kippur,
On the eve of Passover, … on account of … children, … so that … they would not … sleep … And … the eve of Yom Kippur, … so that … would … feed their children.

On the eve of Passover, he would stop on account of the children, so that they would go to sleep during the day, so that they would not be tired and sleep at night. And on the eve of Yom Kippur, he would stop so that his students would remember to feed their children.

p: A man is obligated to gladden his children and the members of his household on a Festival,
“And you shall rejoice on your Festival,
men with what is fit for them and women with what is fit for them.
Men with what is fit for them,

“And you shall sacrifice peace-offerings and you shall eat there and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God”
And now that the Temple is not standing
“And wine that gladdens the heart of man”
brine [moraysa] that was in Tzippori was the same
as the log in the Temple, and with it
